
=== MANA BASE (25 front-face lands + 0 MDFC land-backs, 1 truly tapped) ===
  TRULY TAPPED: Starting Town
  accelerants counted: 4  (restricted, excluded: none)

--- sources model (colour), worst lines (8000 sims over 3 reps, seed 17) ---
  T2 {W}{W}        21.5% ±0.6   Grand Abolisher
  T1 {W}           32.1% ±0.6   Authority of the Consuls
  T1 {U}           33.1% ±0.4   An Offer You Can't Refuse, Opt
  T2 {R}{W}        55.1% ±0.5   Boros Charm
  T6 {G}{G}        58.3% ±0.5   Rampaging Baloths

--- play simulation, 20000 trials over 3 reps, seed 17 ---
  line                                             on play     on draw        baseline(any N on TN)
  Grand Abolisher T2                              8.6±0.3%   10.4±0.1%     93.3±0.2% / 95.8±0.0%
  Authority of the Consuls T1                    32.5±0.4%   36.1±0.3%     98.3±0.0% / 98.8±0.1%
  An Offer You Can't Refuse T1                   32.5±0.4%   36.1±0.3%     98.3±0.0% / 98.8±0.1%
  Boros Charm T2                                 28.7±0.5%   33.1±0.2%     93.3±0.2% / 95.8±0.0%
  Rampaging Baloths T6                           54.9±0.0%   66.1±0.7%     57.2±0.2% / 68.7±0.6%
  Terra, Magical Adept on curve                  77.3±0.3%   83.1±0.1%     87.6±0.3% / 92.2±0.1%

  Diagnosis: a line CLOSE to its baseline is a QUANTITY problem (no land swap will help).
  A line FAR BELOW its baseline is a COLOUR problem (a filter land for that pip is the answer).
  A gap smaller than the two ± beside it is noise, not a finding.

  No mulligan is modelled: every opening seven is kept, so the figures above are FLOORS.
  11.4% of opening sevens hold at most one land (1.6% hold none), off 25 lands in 59.
  Those hands are kept here and shipped back in real play. The share moves with
  land count, so it skews deck-to-deck comparison and not just the level.
